title: Cerulean Pharma - KMS, RBAC & Hosted vs Private Deployment Sync
summary: Introductory security posture discussion focused on KMS/CMK ownership, RBAC model for multi-team access, SSO/SAML integration, audit logging retention and hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs. Customer flagged regulatory data residency and preferred bring-your-own-key for sensitive PHI workflows.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (CTO Cerulean), Jules (Security Lead), Elena (Head of Data), Omar (Infra), Anita (Legal)

Summary (auto): Brief orient on security constraints for PHI workloads, BYOK needs, logging retention, SSO integration, and host vs private deployment options.

00:00 Alex: Okay everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Samir who may pop in around the architecture bits. How's everyone doing?
00:09 Mark: Doing well thanks, excited to dig in. We've got a few objectives; Jules will lead from security side.
00:15 Jules: Hi, yeah thanks. We're primarily here to understand how Redwood can meet our compliance needs — we run a mix of research data and patient derived data so PHI concerns are top of mind.
00:27 Priya: Great, we'll walk through our options — hosted, dedicated, private — and focus on KMS, RBAC, SSO and audit log retention. Quick question: do you already have a KMS/HSM provider you prefer?
00:39 Jules: We use AWS KMS for most things, but for some regulated workflows we want BYOK with an HSM attested key. So the ability to bring keys and control rotation is a must.
00:50 Priya: Understood. Redwood supports BYOK via customer-managed CMKs — you can either supply a KMS key in your VPC for Private deployments or we can integrate with your cloud KMS for Dedicated/Hosted with strict controls. For hosted, note there are additional contractual steps for BYOK and HSM attestation.
01:10 Omar: Wait, for hosted you mean Redwood manages the key or you integrate to our KMS? Which one is typical?
01:16 Priya: For typical hosted setups customers give us a key-wrapping key with limited operations, but for Cerulean we can explore a model where the key stays in your account and we use cross-account access only in Private or Dedicated flows. Hosted can be done but depends on the risk assessment and legal OK.
01:34 Jules: That's helpful. Also, required audit evidence — we need to know where logs live and retention windows. We have a 7-year retention policy for certain audit logs under our regulatory regime. Does Redwood support long-term retention and export?
01:47 Alex: Yes — we stream audit logs to customer destinations (S3, Splunk, Elastic) and you can set retention policies on your side. For hosted customers we also provide an audit bundle for SOC2 evidence, but if you need raw system-level logs for 7 years we recommend private or dedicated with direct log streaming.
02:07 Elena: For the PHI workloads, we may need the compute to reside in our VPC. So the Private deployment option is attractive, but we also want the RBAC model to allow product teams access to only the endpoints they need. How granular is your RBAC?
02:21 Priya: Our RBAC supports role-based scopes per-organization, per-route, and per-model. You can create teams, grant model invocation vs admin privileges, and integrate with your SSO for group mapping. Some customers also use mTLS for service-to-service calls inside their VPC.
02:38 Jules: Do you support SAML SCIM for provisioning? We don't want to hand-manage users.
02:43 Priya: Yes — SAML for SSO and SCIM for user/group provisioning. We map SCIM groups to Redwood roles. There's occasionally a sync mismatch — sometimes display names don't line up — transcription note: we've seen SCIM provisioning with Azure AD, Okta, and Ping.
02:59 Anita (Legal): On encryption at rest and in transit — do you offer customer-controlled keys for model artifacts and KV caches? We need to show encryption for persisted caches.
03:10 Priya: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we encrypt model artifacts and caches. For Private deployments, you can mount encrypted volumes with your KMS. For hosted, we encrypt with our keys by default but offer envelope encryption with customer wrapping keys for sensitive artifacts. (slight stutter) Also for KV cache, we have options to cache on encrypted ephemeral storage or use external KV stores behind your VPC.
03:40 Mark: You mentioned KV cache...what about leakage risk? We don't want prompts from one tenant to leak to another.
03:47 Priya: We do tenant isolation at the runtime layer and logical cache partitioning. In Dedicated and Private deployments there's physical isolation across GPU pools. In hosted there's strict namespace isolation but we do recommend Dedicated for high-sensitivity workloads.
04:03 Mark: Makes sense. Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001? We need certificates and the latest report.
04:09 Alex: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We'll share the attestation and our latest SOC2 report under an NDA. I'll link the security packet after the call.
04:20 Jules: One more — are there retention controls for request/response payloads? We need the option to redact or not persist full text for certain classes of data.
04:30 Priya: We support per-route retention policies: ephemeral mode (no persistence), short-term retention, and long-term retention. For ephemeral, logs are not stored beyond transient buffers, but you can still stream events to your SIEM. Redaction can be applied at our gateway or you can handle it client-side prior to sending.
04:52 Omar: For private deployment networking — how does egress work? We need to make sure nothing routes out of our VPC except to our logging/storage endpoints.
05:02 Priya: Private deployments are customer network-hosted; you control NAT and egress. Redwood's control plane keeps management connection minimal and can be configured with IP allowlists. We'll provide a network diagram and required ports.
05:16 Alex: I'll add the network flow diagram to the follow-up pack.
05:21 Jules: On key rotation — we prefer rotation cadence every 90 days for certain PHI keys, and dual-control for key deletion. Is that supported?
05:31 Priya: We support rotation policies and can configure automated rotate-without-downtime for CMKs. For BYOK in Private deployments, rotation is managed by your KMS; for hosted, Redwood coordinates rotations via a key wrapping approach and key epochs. Dual-control deletions will likely require procedural proof and at least one live operation from your side.
05:51 Mark: Do you do penetration tests and vulnerability scans?
05:55 Alex: Yes, regular penetration tests; summary results included in our security pack. We also have a bug bounty program.
06:03 Jules: Good. We also need to map which teams get access: research, prod, compliance. Do you support scoped API keys and per-key usage tracking?
06:12 Priya: Yes per-token scopes and token-level auditing in the console. You can create tokens with model and route restrictions and view usage tables with token-level cost and latency.
06:24 Elena: For evidence during audits, can we get a tamper-evident log of admin changes?
06:29 Priya: Audit logs include admin actions, role changes, and API key events. We can provide a signed bundle for specific time ranges. For higher assurance, private deployments write logs directly to your storage with immutability policies.
06:43 Anita: Are archived logs immutable for the 7-year window?
06:47 Alex: If you stream logs to your S3 with object lock / WORM enabled you can achieve immutability. Redwood's hosted offering alone can't offer multi-year immutability within our bucket unless you bring your own storage.
07:00 Jules: Understood. Another thing: we have segmentation requirements — some teams cannot access models trained on PHI. Is model governance supported?
07:10 Priya: You can separate model catalogs per-tenant/namespace and restrict model assignment via RBAC. Our Optimize tooling can annotate model quality but governance controls sit with your admin.
07:22 Mark: On performance — for private we need SLA-like guarantees; do you provide latency SLOs?
07:27 Alex: Dedicated and Private come with explicit throughput and latency targets in contract, with credits for breaches. Hosted has best-effort SLAs. We'll put specifics in the proposal.
07:39 Omar: Network details again — what ports and IP ranges for control plane?
07:43 Priya: We'll send a diagram; minimal egress to four endpoints, allowlistable. Some customers lock to specific ASN ranges.
07:51 Mark: Are you able to run in our GCP region in eu-west3? Data residency matters.
07:57 Alex: We have regions in GCP and AWS and can deploy private in your region. Hosted availability depends on region coverage; Dedicated has flexible region options.
08:08 Jules: For SSO — we use Okta. Provisioning and de-provisioning must be immediate for terminated contractors. How fast is SCIM deprovisioning?
08:18 Priya: SCIM pushes are near-real time; deprovisioning within a minute, but there can be a caching window for sessions. We recommend short session TTLs for high-security teams.
08:29 Mark: Any known issues with Okta?
08:31 Priya: Mostly name vs email mapping issues that we help tune during onboarding.
08:36 Anita: Regarding contractual terms for hosted vs private — will Redwood accept clause for customer audits and on-site audits?
08:43 Alex: For enterprise contracts we support customer audits (remote) and on-site usually for dedicated/private with notice. We'll include audit provisions in the contract.
08:55 Jules: One technical nit — we want to ensure model weights never persist in unencrypted form outside our control. If you pull an open model into the cluster, how is it stored?
09:05 Priya: Model artifacts are stored in encrypted volumes and access-controlled storage. For private we can mount your storage so artifacts remain under your control. For hosted, we encrypt with our KMS and can offer envelope encryption with your wrap key for extra control.
09:22 Mark: Great. Can you outline the most likely path: start with Hosted for non-PHI, Dedicated for prod-lax, Private for PHI?
09:31 Alex: That's a common pattern. Many customers start Hosted for evaluation, then Dedicated for predictable performance, and Private for regulated workloads. But we can also pilot Private for a subset if you need VPC-only.
09:43 Jules: We're leaning to pilot Dedicated for non-PHI and a Private proof-of-concept for PHI. What do you need from us to size the private cluster?
09:52 Priya: We'll need expected QPS, model candidate list (model sizes), average and max context lengths, and expected concurrency per route. Also data residency region and preferred GPU types.
10:05 Omar: I'll pull the QPS and model list and send to Alex.
10:10 Mark: Timeline — we hope to have a compliance decision by end of November and pilot in December. Is that feasible?
10:18 Alex: Yes that's feasible. We'll target SOC2 artifacts to help you move faster.
10:22 (brief cross talk)
10:27 Alex: Okay let's capture action items — (recap) we'll send security packet with SOC2/ISO, network diagram, BYOK guide, and propose a date for private architecture deep dive.
10:37 Jules: Please include cost estimate ranges for Dedicated vs Private based on a small pilot (2-4 GPU nodes).
10:45 Priya: We'll include a rough cost and a more detailed SOW for full deployment.
10:49 Anita: We'll review legal terms and follow up on data processing agreement details.
10:54 Alex: Great thank you everyone. We'll follow up with those artifacts and schedule the deep dive.
11:00 Mark: Thanks, bye.
